## About Me  

I am a data scientist and recent Columbia University M.S. graduate in Environmental Health Data Science. Before graduate school, I worked in vaccine development for HIV-1 and COVID-19. I hold a BA in Environmental Biology from Washington University in St. Louis. 

My work applies time-to-event and regression methods to real world health data, including an open source R package for survival analysis on high-dimensional datasets and a thesis analyzing environmental exposures and prostate cancer severity. I'm looking to bring my methodological background into a real-world evidence role, deriving insights from EHR, claims, and clinical data to inform treatment decisions.

## ExpoMet: an R package for exposome- and metabolome-wide association studies

Expomet is freely available on Github (https://github.com/haotianwu17/ExpoMet) and will be added to CRAN shortly. The package vignette can be found under the project tab.

## Thesis: "The environmental chemical exposome and prostate cancer severity: Race-stratified associations in a race balanced cohort"
### with Dr. Haotian Wu at Columbia University

My thesis investigates the associations between environmental chemical exposures and prostate cancer diagnosis and aggressiveness using high-dimensional epidemiological data. The analysis applies GWAS-style regression across 5,000+ chemical features, with covariate adjustment for key demographic and clinical factors. My work found that chemical exposures, including endocrine-disrupting compounds, may be associated with prostate cancer severity.

This project uses high-dimensional data analysis, regression modeling, principal component analysis, multiple testing correction, and mixture methods.
